title: Step-by-Step Guide: Kinetrol EL Positioner Calibration Procedure
summary: Learn how to easily calibrate your Kinetrol EL Electropneumatic Positioner. This guide covers the automatic end-stop finding procedure, feedback potentiometer reset, and essential field setup steps.
content:
The Advantage of Kinetrol EL Positioners

The Kinetrol EL (Electropneumatic) Positioner is highly regarded in the process control industry for its rapid, user-friendly field setup. Unlike legacy mechanical positioners that require complex linkage adjustments and zero/span screw tweaking, the Kinetrol EL utilizes an advanced microprocessor to perform an automatic end-stop finding procedure.

Using just three push buttons (SET, UP, and DOWN) and intuitive LED indicators, technicians can calibrate the positioner to the physical limits of the actuator in a matter of minutes. Below is the official step-by-step calibration procedure.

Prerequisites for Calibration

Before beginning the calibration sequence, ensure you have the following:

  • A stable instrument air supply connected to the positioner (meeting ISO8573-1 Class 5.5.5 standards).
  • A 4-20mA signal generator or active control loop connected to the input terminals.
  • The actuator must be free to stroke fully from 0% to 100% without mechanical obstruction.

Step 1: Establishing the 0% Baseline

The positioner must first establish its physical starting point before the automatic sweep begins.

  1. Turn on the air supply to the actuator.
  2. Apply an input signal of below 4 mA (e.g., 3.8 mA or simply disconnect the signal). This forces the actuator vane to rest firmly against its mechanical 0% (closed) end-stop.
  3. Once the actuator is resting at 0%, temporarily turn off the air supply pressure.
  4. Now, increase the input signal to above 4 mA (e.g., 12 mA). The positioner is now electrically active but pneumatically disabled.

Step 2: Entering Setup Mode

With the signal active and air off, you will now instruct the microprocessor to enter calibration mode.

  • Locate the three push buttons on the positioner circuit board.
  • Press and hold both the SET and UP buttons simultaneously.
  • The LEDs on the board will indicate that the positioner has successfully entered Setup Mode.
  • Turn the air supply back on.

Step 3: The Automatic End-Stop Sweep

Now that the unit is in Setup Mode and pressurized, you will trigger the automatic calibration sequence.

  • Press the SET and UP buttons simultaneously one more time.
  • The calibration LED will begin to flash. At this point, remove your hands and let the microprocessor take over.
  • The actuator will automatically stroke towards its 100% (fully open) end-stop. Upon reaching the physical limit, it will pause.
  • It will then steadily move downscale back to the 0% end-stop, pause again, and finally return to the position corresponding to your current mA input signal.
  • Success: The calibration data (the exact physical limits of the actuator's stroke) is automatically written to the positioner's non-volatile memory. The calibration is complete.

Advanced: Resetting the Feedback Potentiometer

If you have recently performed mechanical maintenance, replaced the actuator vane, or rebuilt the positioner, the internal feedback potentiometer may be out of alignment. You must reset it before performing the automatic sweep above.

  1. Ensure the actuator vane is resting at its mechanical 0% end-stop.
  2. Press the UP button repeatedly until the POT LED lights up continuously.
  3. Once the POT LED is solid, proceed with the Automatic End-Stop Sweep (Steps 1 through 3). The positioner will re-sync the physical stroke with the potentiometer's electrical resistance range.

Conclusion

The Kinetrol EL Positioner's automatic calibration routine drastically reduces commissioning time and eliminates human error during setup. Note: If you are calibrating an Intrinsically Safe (IS) version, always adhere strictly to the ATEX/IECEx safety guidelines outlined in the official Kinetrol TD 120 manual.
